Morshed Ahmed Khan, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 

Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, Advocate—For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Jannatul Maowa Runa and others ------------ Petitioners 
Vs.
AHM Roushan Ali Miah and others ----------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
5. The case of the pre-emptor as has been set out in this revisional application in precise is that, the case land originally belonged to one, Mofiz Pramanik and Mosirunesa. After the demise of Mosirunessa her husband, Mofiz inherited the property. While Mofiz had been enjoying title and possession over that land he transferred 10 decimals of land to one, Korban Ali on 4-9-1984. The pre-emptor then purchased 5 decimals of lands from Korban Ali on 26-11-1997 and thereby he became the co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. In further development, one Akbar Ali, the opposite party No. 4 to the pre-emption case, transferred 17 decimals of land to the opposite party No. 3 by disputed kabala that registered on 11-9-2001 though without serving any notice upon the pre-emptor-opposite party though the purchaser pre-emptees is the stranger-purchaser to the case holding. Pre-emptor came to learn about the disputed transfer on 3-10-2001 and after obtaining the certified copy of the said deed on 4-10-2011 filed the instant pre-emption case on 29-1-2002. It has further been stated in the petition for pre-emption that, if the pre-emptor had the knowledge about the said transaction. he would have purchased the same. Since the pre-emption case has been filed within the very statutory period of limitation so the pre-emptor is entitled to have the lands through pre-emption and hence the instant case. 

 6. Per contra, the present-petitioner as pre-emptee-purchaser contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations so made in the petition for pre-emption contending, inter alia, that, one Akbar Ali had been in possession over 30 decimals of land on mutating his name in the khatian and while he had been enjoying title and possession over that 30 decimals of land he at first proposed the pre-emptor to sell the case land even the father of the pre-emptees named, Nazrul Islam also proposed the pre-emptor and his son to purchase the land but as they refused to purchase the same, the pre-emptees then purchased the case land by registered kabala dated 11-9-2001. Soon after purchasing the case land, the pre-emptees then started enjoying title and possession over the suit properties by planting various trees that cost Taka 65,000. It has further been stated that, there has been a Madrasha located in the case land though it was not made party in the case. It has then stated that, the vendor, Korban Ali who transferred 5 decimals of land upon purchasing 10 decimals of land had separated his jama before selling 5 decimals of land to the pre-emptor. It has stated in the written objection that, inspite of having no preferential right the pre-emptor filed the case having absolute knowledge about the disputed transfer. It has further been stated that, if the pre-emption case is allowed in that event, the pre-emptee Nos. 1-3 will suffer irreparable loss and injury and therefore the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed. 

 12. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below, the pre-emptees-purchasers as petitioners then came before this court and obtained the instant Rule and order of stay as has been stated hereinabove. 

 17. Conversely, Mr Md Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel appearing for the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 (after the demise of the pre-emptor his heirs were substituted as pre-emptor-opposite party Nos. 1(a)-1(e) vehemently opposes the contention so have been advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioners and contends that, the learned Judges of the courts below have very perfectly allowed the pre-emption case finding that, all the legal requirement enumerated in section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has duly been complied with leaving no reason to interfere with the concurrent judgement and order passed by the learned Judges of the courts below. 

 19. The learned Counsel further submits that, since under the provision of clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act there has been gulf of difference between separation of holding and separation of jama so mere mutating the name in the khatian by the predecessor of the present-pre-emptors will not deprive the pre-emptor to exercise his statutory right of pre-emption to pre-empt the case land. 

 20. The learned Counsel further submits that. though the pre-emptees in its written objection allegedly stated that, before selling 5 decimals of land in favour of the pre-emptor by Korban Ali, he had mutated his name in the khatian vide mutation case but nothing of that sort of document has ever been produced by the said pre-emptees during the process of taking evidence so it clearly shows that, the mutation proceedings so have been alleged by the pre-emptees-petitioners has got no existence in the eye of law. 

 26. However, that very fact so described in the written objection could not be substantiated by any of their witness though as many as 3 witnesses have been produced by the pre-emptees-petitioners, so the point of waiver and acquiescence as alleged by the pre-emptees cannot stand. Though on that very point, the learned Counsel for the petitioners has placed his reliance on the decision reported in 42 DLR (AD) 189 but the facts so have been described and the ratio so have been settled in that very decision is squarely different from that of the facts as has been stated in the instant case. Invariably, the said decision cannot be made applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. 

 27. Now, only point remains, whether the pre-emptor ceased to have any right as a co-sharer by purchase to have the case land by way of purchase. It is alleged by the pre-emptees that, the vendor that is, Korban Ali before transferring 5 decimals of land infavour of the pre-emptees mutated his name in the khatian vide mutation case No. 2762 (9-1) 86/87 dated 11-11-1987 so before transferring the said case land, the khatian since has been spitted up so the pre-emptor cannot claim to be a co-sharer by purchase in the case holding. It has further been claimed by the pre-emptees that, after purchasing the case land even they also mutated their respective name in the khatian vide Mutation Case Nos. 1250, 1251 and 1252 in the year 2001 and 2002. Though there has been no mutation case number ever stated in the written objection but OPW 1 who is the father of pre-emptee purchaser No. 1 and 3 and the father in-law of the pre-emptee No. 2 has deposed that, in the month of March 2002 they got their names mutated in the khatian. 

 30. To support that very submission, the learned Counsel for the petitioner has also placed a slew of decisions. On going through those decisions. I find that their lordship held that, if the holding is separated for paying the rent in that event, the pre-emptor will cease the right to pre-empt the case land in the said holding which is made under clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So, in view of those decisions it has been settled that, mere separating a jama, the pre-emptor will not be deprived to exercise his right of pre-emption. 

 31. To substantiate that very submission, the learned Counsel has also placed his reliance in the decision reported in 18 BLT (HC) 83 where it has clearly been held that, as regards to point of law, the later decisions will always prevail over. Though in the decision reported in 3 ALR 58. the decision so have been given by the Hon'ble Appellate Division on that particular point made under section 117(C) has not been referred even though I find substance in it because in all along the subsequent decision always prevails over. And in the decision reported in 3 ALR it has vividly been discussed how a separation of jama and a separation of holding can be distinguished. Because, under the provision of clause (C) of section 117(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, if any-person wants to separate a holding, in that event several procedure has to be performed but in the process of separating a jama which is generally called mutation in the khatian an application is simply filed before the respective Tohsil Office who then refers the same to the Assistant Commissioner (land) and the Assistant Commissioner land upon performing some procedure just mutates the khatian enabling the applicant to pay the rent in respect of his portion of land by which it cannot be said that separation of holding is held. Moreover, in separating a holding there must have some procedure to be carried out by issuing notice to all the co-sharer of the case holding but nothing of this sort has ever been complied with in the instant case. 

 32. Moreover, as has been stated herein above that, not a scrap of paper has been produced by the pre-emptees in support of separating the holding by the vendor of the pre-emptor though in the written objection the pre-emptees has stated the mutation number separating the jama by the vendor of the pre-emptees named, Korban Ali but that very paper has not been produced by the pre-emptees while giving evidence before the trial court so mere making any assertion in the written objection will not suffice to prove the case of the pre-emptees in absence of any document thereof. 

 37. It has already been held that, in absence of final publication of record of right as provided in section 19 and section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act there cannot be any presumption as to the correctness. In such a view, it can safely construe that, until and unless a khatian is finally published, the pre-emptee cannot claim to have separated the holding, so that very decision is squarely applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case.
